item.title: Lions bring in veteran defensive backs for workouts Monday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Only the Colts have given up more points and yards than the Lions so far this season, so it's not surprising to hear that Detroit is looking for some outside defensive help.
item.content:encoded:
Only the Colts have given up more points and yards than the Lions so far this season, so it's not surprising to hear that Detroit is looking for some outside defensive help.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that the team will have several veteran defensive backs in for workouts on Monday. Jordan Fuller, Jalen Mills, and Mike Edwards are among the players set to participate.

Mills played in three games for the Lions last season. Edwards saw time with the Chiefs while Fuller appeared in six games for the Falcons.

The Lions have safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph on the physically unable to perform list, which means they won't be able to return until Week 5 at the earliest. They lost another safety to injury when Avonte Maddox got hurt last Thursday and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin was also banged up during their loss to the Bills.

item.title: Mike Vrabel didn't want his Sunday ruined by questions about Drake Maye's struggles
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye finished second in the MVP voting in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye finished second in the MVP voting in 2025. This year, he's second from the bottom in passer rating among the quarterbacks who have played two games.

The Week 1 game was bad, with three ill-advised fourth-quarter interceptions. The Week 2 performance wasn't much better, featuring a head-scratching interception after a long completion to receiver Romeo Doubs. Maye finished with 14 completions in 22 attempts for 208 yards and one interception.

After the game, Ben Volin of the Boston Globe asked Vrabel about his concern level with the offense, and whether he's worried Maye is pressing.

"No, just trying to win the game, Ben," Vrabel said. "You’re not gonna ruin my Sunday, but I'll come back to you tomorrow. Thanks, bud."

Greg Bedard of Boston Sports Journal tried to ask a related question. Vrabel cut him off.

"You, neither," Vrabel said. "You're not gonna ruin it, either."

On one hand, Vrabel should be happy. With road trips coming up to Jacksonville and Buffalo, the Patriots desperately needed a win. Still, his reaction shows that, yes, there is something to be worried about with the offense generally, and with Maye specifically.

item.title: Vikings are now the betting favorites to win the NFC North
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North.
item.content:encoded:
Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North. A lot can change in two weeks.

The Vikings are now 2-0, with both wins coming against division opponents, a game ahead of the Lions, Packers and Bears, and the new betting favorites to win the division.

The Vikings' odds are +194 to win what looks to be the NFL's most competitive division. The Lions are next at +205, followed by the Packers at +285. Last year's NFC North winners, the Bears, not have the longest odds, at +500, amid concerns that Caleb Williams could miss extended time with a hamstring injury.

Uncertainty at quarterback in Minnesota is an issue, but the Vikings have found a way to win two weeks in a row with Carson Wentz replacing the injured Kyler Murray. The Vikings' defense looks ferocious, and the Vikings look like a playoff team. Something few thought they'd be just a couple weeks ago.

item.title: Fox audio issues had some viewers watching one game, hearing Vikings-Bears
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience.
item.content:encoded:
The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience.

As noted by Megan Armstrong of Awful Announcing, multiple viewers of the Packers-Jets and Falcons-Panthers games on Fox complained that the sound was replaced with audio from Bears-Vikings.

Armstrong's story includes multiple tweets, including visual/audio evidence.

A PFT reader emailed the same concern.

"My husband and I were watching the Packers/Jets game on FOX today," the reader said. "Twice, we lost the audio for our game and were listening to the Vikings/Bears game. The first time only lasted about a minute but the second time was at least 5-6 minutes. So we're watching the Pack and listening to the Vikes."

In nearly 25 years of doing this, audio from one game making its way into another game is a first. And hopefully it's the last time something like that will happen.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy see the issues with the Pittsburgh offense
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When he's complaining about Anthony Fauci, ESPN, and/or Shailene Woodley, Aaron Rodgers is not subtle.
item.content:encoded:
When he's complaining about Anthony Fauci, ESPN, and/or Shailene Woodley, Aaron Rodgers is not subtle. When he has concerns about his football team, his criticisms are harder to pinpoint.

But they're still there.

After Sunday's loss to the Patriots, Rodgers dropped a hint or two regarding coach Mike McCarthy's offense. And Rodgers did it in a way that will give him plausible deniability if someone else spots it and points it out.

"In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better," Rodgers told reporters after the 20-6 loss. "And that starts with me at like making sure Mike knows what's working, what's not working, our coaches know, and — so we can call stuff that we feel like has a better chance."

In other words, some of the "stuff" McCarthy was calling didn't have a very good chance.

When asked later about things that are "working" and "not working," Rodgers said, "The plays were fine." But he then suggested that perhaps the offense was overloaded with plays.

"If there's too much stuff in the plan, we've got to cut it back," Rodgers said. "I'm always liking to push the envelope, and if I see guys doing it the right way in practice, then I feel good about it, but we've got to transfer the practice to the game obviously and the details gotta come with it."

The hidden criticisms aren't off-base; McCarthy himself made similar comments about the size of the game plan.

"We've got to look at the volume," he told reporters after the game. "That's Marty Schottenheimer, that was his thing. It was a great lesson for a young coach to learn, and here I am some old bastard that didn't do it this week. If it's not clean, you cut the volume down, and we're not clean on offense.

"So the volume is getting cut down. That's the first starting point, and that's my fault. I felt it earlier in the week. We've got a quarterback that could play at any volume of game plan, but at the end of the day, it's a team game. We've got to give Aaron better platforms to throw off of and have the opportunities because I don't want to dink and dunk and play all day and play keep-away football."

McCarthy's remarks on the volume of the game plan came after he attributed the offensive struggles to things he had observed during the week.

"Felt it in practice frankly, coming off of last week," McCarthy said. "As I stated, I felt we were real herky-jerky trying to get in the run and pass. . . . The run game was a little bit herky-jerky. . . . But the reality of it is the detail is not there, and that's on coaching. It starts with me. I'm calling the offense. I have to get the detail better. . . . I felt it on Wednesday and Thursday. I'm a veteran coach. I know better. I didn't do a good job."

McCarthy was asked to clarify his comment about "feeling it" during the week.

"Just volume," McCarthy said. "We've done this a long time. You know when the volume is up, and you know when you're pushing the envelope too. It's also the first year of the staff and players working together. So you want to push your players, but end of the day, you've got to do it to win a game."

Rodgers has faith McCarthy will make the fixes that need to be made.

"I've seen Mike for 14 years. So, Mike is going to take accountability, sometimes when it's not his fault, doesn't need to do that," Rodgers said. "But Mike loves the guys, and he wants us to have some urgency and to bounce back with this, and I know we will."

They need to. The offense has engineered one touchdown drive in two full games, and it covered only 31 yards. The Steelers easily could have lost to the Falcons in Week 1, and the Falcons looked horrible in Week 2.

In six days, the 2-0 Bengals come to Pittsburgh. And while the Steelers tend to find a way to win certain key games, it becomes a much taller task if the offense isn't delivering.

At some point, Rodgers himself has to deliver. He's completing fewer than 60 percent of his passes (his career average is 65.1), he's averaging only 5.2 yards per attempt (down from 6.7 in 2025), and his passer rating is a very sluggish 72.1. Rodgers has never had a full-season rating below 90.5, and that happened during his 5-12 final year with the Jets.

item.title: Troy Aikman thought he'd have a new deal with ESPN by now
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Monday night, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call the Giants-Rams game.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday night, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call the Giants-Rams game. Buck has a new contract. Aikman does not.

And Aikman is surprised that his new deal is not yet done.

Via Jon Lewis of SportsMediaWatch.com, Aikman recently addressed the situation in an appearance on the Sports Media Podcast with Richard Deitsch.

“I thought something would be done prior to the start of this season,” Aikman told Deitsch. “I’ve never gone into the last year of a contract ever since I signed with the Dallas Cowboys. And so I thought that it would be done. It’s not. When it might get done, if it gets done, is anyone’s guess. And it’s really not something that I’m putting a lot of energy into.”

Buck and Aikman have worked together since 2002. They jumped from Fox to ESPN in 2022. They signed five-year deals. Buck now has a five-year extension; Aikman does not.

Aikman said that he hasn't spoken with ESPN executives regarding what Buck's deal means to Aikman's.

“How much of that is my decision, I guess is yet to be determined,” Aikman said. “Would I like to continue working with Joe Buck moving down the road? 100 percent."

Perhaps ESPN will decide to pair Buck with someone else, like Pat McAfee. (I'm kidding, I think.) However it goes, Aikman realizes that the broader mission of ESPN pilfering Buck and Aikman from Fox has been accomplished.

“I came over in 2022 in large part to kind of help mend the relationship with ESPN and the NFL,” Aikman said. “I feel like the reason that I was brought over, I fulfilled whatever obligations they were expecting from me. So much so that . . . the league now owns 10 percent of the network. So I would say the fence has been mended."

The only question left is whether the bridge with Aikman will eventually be burned.

item.title: Shane Steichen on 9 straight losses: We're right there, have to find a way to win at the end
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026.

“We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher,” Irsay-Gordon said at her press conference after announcing that Ballard and Steichen would both return.

But with Sunday’s overtime loss to Kansas City, Indianapolis has now lost nine consecutive games dating back to Week 12 of last season. The team finished 8-9 after starting 8-2 and has now dropped the first two this season.

A lot has happened along the way — including starting quarterback Daniel Jones going down with a torn Achilles. But in a results-oriented business, Indianapolis has not been good enough.

At the end of his postgame press conference on Sunday night, Steichen was asked what he tells the team after nine consecutive losses.

“I tell them to keep your freaking heads up, dude,” Steichen said. “It is a long season ahead of us. We are battling like crazy. That’s the message. We have to continue to grow and learn. There is a lot of football left. Like I said last week, we are right there. We have to find a way to win at the end. That was one of those games.

“It is a freaking hard-ass league, and you have got to find a way to win these tight games.”

The Colts will be back at home next weekend to face a division rival, the 0-2 Texans.

item.title: Report: Saints LT Kelvin Banks believed to have a high-ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle.

Kelvin Banks was carted off during the 24-17 win and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Banks is believed to have a high-ankle sprain. Banks is set to have an MRI to evaluate the extent of the injury.

High-ankle sprains often keep players out for weeks, so a stint on injured reserve could be in the cards for the 2025 first-round pick.

Asim Richards replaced Banks after he hurt his ankle on Sunday and is in line to take over as the starter for any future absences.

item.title: Bears had second biggest scoring dip ever from Week 1 to Week 2
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In Week 1, the Bears came within one point of scoring 60.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 1, the Bears came within one point of scoring 60. In Week 2, they came within three points of scoring none.

The dip from 59 points to start the season to only a field goal in the second game is, per NBC Sports research, the second biggest turnaround from Week 1 to Week 2 in NFL history.

In 1973, the Falcons opened the season with a 62-7 win over the Saints. The following week, they lost to the Rams, 31-0.

That year, Falcons quarterback Dick Shiner went from completing 13 of 15 passes for 227 yards and three touchdowns to completing two of nine for 17 yards and an interception. (The Falcons finished the year 9-5 but missed the playoffs.)

On Sunday, the weather — and the Minnesota defense — had something to do with the reduction in production. Still, it won't be easy to get closer to 59 than three if quarterback Caleb Williams misses time with the hamstring injury he suffered in the fourth quarter.

item.title: Dallas Turner beat TE Colston Loveland for decisive sack
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Vikings defensive end Dallas Turner has blossomed into one of the best pass rushers in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings defensive end Dallas Turner has blossomed into one of the best pass rushers in the NFL. He had two sacks on Sunday at Chicago, to go with the sack he had last week against the Packers.

The last sack came on the last play of the day, slamming the door on a potential game-winning touchdown from backup quarterback Tyson Bagent.

On the play, Turner bull rushed Bears tight end Colston Loveland, riding Loveland all the way to Bagent.

After the game, I asked Turner by phone why the Bears thought they could slow him down with a tight end. He said the attack crafted by defensive coordinator Brian Flores dictates the approach, by creating the kind of chaos that forces the offense into unfavorable matchups.

Turner said that, on several plays during the final drive, a tight end was trying to block him.

The effort was just the latest example of Turner's arrival as an elite pass rusher. He said that his recent success is a "progressive thing," based on the time he has spent in the Flores defense, and not the result of any specific moment where the light went on.

He turned the lights out for the Bears on Sunday, propelling the Vikings to 2-0 with an unlikely 9-3 win in Chicago — Minnesota's seventh straight win at Soldier Field.

item.title: Kirk Cousins throws three TDs, Raiders start 2-0 with 26-14 victory over Chargers
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Klint Kubiak is the first Raiders coach to start his tenure 2-0 since Bill Callahan in 2002.
item.content:encoded:
You like that?

Raiders fans all over might be chanting Kirk Cousins' unofficial slogan for at least the next week after the quarterback threw for three more touchdowns, powering Las Vegas to a 26-14 victory to begin the season 2-0.

The Raiders had not started the season with two consecutive wins since 2021.

Las Vegas played solid defense against Los Angeles, picking up some timely takeaways. Omarion Hampton had another game-changing fumble, coughing the ball up on a fourth-quarter run up the middle with the Chargers down by three.

The Raiders scored a couple of plays later with Cousins’ third touchdown pass, going up by 10 with 2:59 on the clock.

After Justin Herbert’s second interception of the game, Joe Alt closed what was a particularly bad day with a holding penalty in the end zone for a safety to close out the scoring.

Alt had previously been flagged for three false start penalties, despite the Chargers playing at home.

Herbert finished the contest 15-of-27 for 192 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He also had three of the Chargers’ six fumbles on the day, though the team did not lose possession on any of them.

Hampton had 94 yards on 23 carries with a touchdown.

But on the other side, Cousins was 19-of-29 for 253 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. Tre Tucker was his top target, catching five passes for 119 yards. Two of Tucker’s catches went for at least 40 yards, including a long touchdown in the first quarter to open the scoring.

Cousins is now just the second quarterback in franchise history to have at least three touchdown passes in each of the club’s first two games, joining Ken Stabler from 1976.

Kubiak has become the fourth coach in franchise history to win each of his first two games, joining Al Davis, John Madden, and Bill Callahan.

At 2-0, the Raiders will again be on the road in Week 3 as they play the Saints in New Orleans.

The schedule doesn’t get easier for the 0-2 Chargers, as they’ll be on the road to face the Bills in Week 3.

item.title: Saints rally for 24-17 upset of Ravens
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Saints fell behind the Lions 21-0 in the season opener but rallied to force overtime.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints fell behind the Lions 21-0 in the season opener but rallied to force overtime. They lost on a failed 2-point conversion.

They trailed the Ravens 14-3 in the first half and 17-9 in the second. They did not lose.

Tyler Shough directed the Saints to a 24-17 comeback win over the Ravens.

The Saints outscored the Ravens 14-0 in the fourth quarter as Shough threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave and ran for a 1-yard touchdown on fourth down with 1:28 remaining. The Saints outgained the Ravens 137 to 43 in the fourth quarter, with Baltimore getting only two first downs.

In four possessions in the second half, the Ravens got no closer to the end zone than the Saints 31.

Shough's touchdown run was reviewed and upheld on replay. Two downs earlier, replay upheld officials' on-field ruling that tight end Juwan Johnson came up just short of the goal line on a diving attempt after a reception from Shough.

The Saints still had to hold off the Ravens, and Lamar Jackson got Baltimore to the New Orleans 37 with 20 seconds left. Saints safety Julian Blackmon intercepted Jackson on a desperation throw toward Rashod Bateman at the 7.

Shough went 27-of-34 for 252 yards and a touchdown and ran for 23 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. The Saints rushed for only 65 yards on 27 carries.

They were 8-of-15 on third down and 2-of-2 on fourth.

The Ravens, who had 228 yards at halftime, finished with 312 yards. Jackson was 21-of-31 for 235 yards with a touchdown and an interception, and he ran for 34 yards on four carries.

Derrick Henry ran for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, and Bateman caught seven passes for 88 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Bengals stymie Texans 20-6 as Houston drops first two games again
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bengals defense is not the same defense as last season.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals defense is not the same defense as last season.

The Texans were 0-for-4 in the red zone, with their only points coming on two field goals, and the Bengals won 20-6.

Cincinnati ran its record to 2-0 in 2026, only the third time in its history that it has started 2-0. Houston lost its first two games for a second consecutive season. The Texans rallied from an 0-3 start last season to make the playoffs.

The Bengals sacked C.J. Stroud four times, with Cedric Johnson getting two and Jonathan Allen and Shemar Stewart each getting one. The Texans were 5-of-17 on third down and 0-for-4 on fourth down, and they gained only 60 yards on 18 carries as prize offseason acquisition David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries.

Stroud led the Texans in rushing 29 yards on three carries.

Stroud threw a career-high 55 passes, completing 30 for 353 yards without his three top receivers. Nico Collins was inactive; Jayden Higgins is on season-ending injured reserve; and Tank Dell is still working his way back from his 2024 leg injury.

The Bengals had only 267 yards and punted eight times, and Joe Burrow was sacked five times. But Burrow, who was limited in two practices last week with a back injury, threw touchdown passes of 32 and 18 yards to Ja'Marr Chase. Chase, who had only two catches for 12 yards in the season opener, caught seven passes for 75 yards. Tee Higgins made five receptions for 95 yards.

Chase Brown ran 20 times for 80 yards.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: No regrets about how we handled end of regulation against Packers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.
item.content:encoded:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.

After the 20-17 loss, Glenn said he never considered calling a timeout when the Packers faced a fourth down near midfield with about a minute left in regulation. The Packers wound up running the clock down and taking a delay of game penalty before trying a Hail Mary on the final snap of the game.

On Sunday, Glenn said he didn't want the team's offense to be backed up after a punt and reiterated that on a Monday video conference while expressing no doubt about the course of action he chose for the team.

"Between me and our game management guys, our analytical guys, we talk through those situations quite a bit," Glenn said. "That situation actually came up in a number of our conversations. When we have the punter at the logo, we don't want to put ourselves in a situation where we get our guys in a backed up situation. I know we talk about getting our offense going in that situation, but the thing is they had two timeouts also. If you put yourself in a backed up situation and things don't go as planned, I think you’re giving the other team an opportunity to go out there and make a play. I just felt like that was the right decision to do at that point and we actually wanted to play for overtime when it came to that.”

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Sunday that he was "really confused" by how Glenn handled the situation, which could be translated to being really thankful that Glenn allowed the Packers to control how the final minute of regulation played out.

item.title: Aaron Glenn on Jets taking the ball in OT: I wanted to control the clock
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.

Glenn chose not to use his final timeouts before the end of regulation, which was questioned by many because the Jets had a chance to get the ball back and end the contest without needing to go into extra time. After the game went into overtime, Glenn made another decision that came up for further inspection.

The Jets won the toss and opted to receive the kickoff. Quarterback Geno Smith was sacked on the first two plays and the Jets never got the ball back after punting because the Packers drove for a game-winning field goal. After the game, Glenn said he was hoping to leave the Packers with as little time on offense as possible.

"Usually, if you can get yourself in a situation like that and you can really control the clock, you can control exactly how they're going to play offense once you go and score," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "So, we control the clock, we go run it down; say we run it seven minutes, which we’ve done before, we've run a number of time off the clock, it only gives them so much time to try to rebuttal. We didn’t do a good job in that situation. And plus, to me, once you get the ball and you go down and score, you put the pressure on the other team that has to go ahead and score. But that didn’t happen for us the way I planned."

Having Smith drop back to pass is a curious way to control the clock, although the Jets had struggled to find momentum running the ball all afternoon. They had held the Packers' offense in check, however, and Green Bay ended the afternoon with 199 total yards, but Glenn went with his offense and that turned out to be the wrong choice.

item.title: Broncos rally for 20-13 win over Jaguars
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Broncos wiped out a 10-point deficit on their way to their first win.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos offense took a big step forward in the final quarter of Sunday's home game against the Broncos.

After being limited to 16 points through the first seven quarters of the season, the Broncos found themselves down 13-3 to the Jaguars in the fourth quarter. They responded with a pair of touchdown drives in the fourth quarter to take a 20-13 lead over the Jaguars and then put together an impressive four-minute offense to run out the clock on their first win of the season.

Quarterback Bo Nix converted one third down with a 29-yard strike to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman picked up another one with a 12-yard run that forced the Jaguars to use their final timeout. Coleman was pressed into duty with RJ Harvey inactive and J.K. Dobbins leaving with a hamstring injury, and the fourth-round pick came through with one more big run to allow the Broncos to run out the clock.

Coleman also scored the go-ahead touchdown run with 7:21 left to play. It was his first NFL score and he finished the day with 10 carries for 39 yards.

That score came after Jaguars kicker Cam Little missed a 54-yard field goal and the first Broncos touchdown came after cornerback Riley Moss picked off Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Waddle had two catches on that touchdown drive and finished the day with eight catches for 138 yards.

That's the impact Denver was looking for when they traded for Waddle this offseason and it helped get Bo Nix on track after a bad interception in the end zone to kill a first half scoring chance. Nix finished 22-of-31 for 288 yards and a touchdown to tight end Nate Adkins.

Neither team scored in the first quarter, but the Jaguars got a touchdown to open the second quarter and took a 10-3 lead into halftime. They extended it to 13-3, but the interception and missed field goal opened the door for the Broncos. Denver's defense forced a punt after Coleman's touchdown put them ahead and the offense was able to slam the door.

That's a good development for offensive coordinator Davis Mills and the Broncos will now turn their attention to a Sunday night game against the Rams. The Jaguars will try to stop the bleeding at home against the Patriots.

item.description: Ja'Marr Chase scored his second touchdown of the day, on an 18-yard pass from Joe Burrow.
item.content:encoded:
Ja'Marr Chase scored his second touchdown of the day, on an 18-yard pass from Joe Burrow.

The Bengals lead 17-3 with 3:03 remaining in the third quarter.

Chase, who had only two catches for 12 yards in the season opener, has six receptions for 70 yards. His first touchdown covered 32 yards as he made a poster catch around Texans cornerback Derek Stingley.

Chase caught two passes for 26 yards in Week 1 of 2025 before14 receptions for 165 yards and a touchdown the following week against the Jaguars.

Burrow, who was limited in two of the three practices last week with a back injury, is 17-of-25 for 179 yards and two touchdowns.

item.title: Todd Monken: "'Browns are gonna Browns' — f—k that"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: When NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted JuJu Smith-Schuster and said, “Browns is the Browns” after the team’s embarrassing 34-10 loss to open the season, Cleveland head coach Todd Monken said he didn’t see it that way.
item.content:encoded:
When NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted JuJu Smith-Schuster and said, “Browns is the Browns” after the team’s embarrassing 34-10 loss to open the season, Cleveland head coach Todd Monken said he didn’t see it that way.

He was a little more emphatic after the club’s 23-19 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

“Browns are gonna Browns — fuck that, OK?” Monken said. “The guys took that to heart.”

That was Monken’s walk-off message in his press conference and the end to an answer about how his team was able to stay warm and motivated during the long weather delay.

Monken also noted — before the expletive — that practice earlier in the week got chippy.

“We had a couple of scuffles Wednesday — which is good,” Monken said. “It’s awesome, because guys didn’t like it. They were a little pissed off, right? You ought to be a little pissed off. Played awful. It wasn’t the standard.”

The Browns played a lot better on Sunday.

We’ll see if Monken can talk that same talk after next week’s matchup against the Panthers.

item.title: Dan Quinn: Commanders are bummed for Jayden Daniels, will rally around Marcus Mariota
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Daniels suffered a dislocation to his left (non-throwing) elbow.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders don't yet know how serious Jayden Daniels' elbow injury is, but the tone of coach Dan Quinn's post-game comments suggested that Daniels will be out for a while.

Quinn talked about the importance of supporting both Daniels and backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, who finished today's game against the Cowboys and will apparently be starting for the Commanders next week.

"He did injure his left elbow, it was a dislocation. X-rays showed no fracture. He'll travel back home with the team. More imaging tomorrow," Quinn said after the game. "Man, are we bummed for him. I thought he was really playing his ass off. And we will rally so hard around Marcus until Jayden is back."

It's the second year in a row that Daniels has dislocated his non-throwing elbow. Last year, Daniels missed four weeks with the injury, returned for one game, re-aggravated the elbow in that game, and then missed the final four weeks of the season.

How much time Daniels misses now remains to be seen, but Quinn summed Daniels' injury up by saying, "It sucks."

item.title: Eagles need last-minute comeback to beat Titans 24-20
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: It wasn't easy, but the Eagles pulled out a win in Tennessee.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles were expected to beat the Titans easily today in Tennessee. Philadelphia won, but it wasn't easy.

The Titans were competitive throughout the game and took a 20-17 lead with two minutes to go, but the Eagles came back with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with Jalen Hurts hitting Darius Cooper in the end zone for the game-winning touchdown in a 24-20 victory.

The Eagles got next to nothing from Saquon Barkley, who was injured on Philadelphia's first offensive snap, missed the rest of the first half, and was limited in the second half. Barkley finished with four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward showed promise, completing 13 of 20 passes for 183 yards and also running for two touchdowns. The game ended, however, with Ward setting up to throw a Hail Mary and getting nowhere close.

The Eagles are 2-0, but neither win has been particularly impressive. The Titans are 0-2, but they have to feel like today's game showed progress.

item.title: Patriots shut down Steelers' offense, win 20-3
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Aaron Rodgers could do nothing today in New England.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers' offense was putrid today against the Patriots, with Aaron Rodgers able to do nothing in a 20-3 loss.

It was an ugly performance by Pittsburgh that will raise serious questions about whether Rodgers, in what he says is his final NFL season, is going to be able to lead them to anything better than mediocrity.

Today, the Steelers were sub-mediocre. Rodgers managed just 187 yards on 23-of-39 passing, with no touchdowns and one interception, and he also lost a fumble that New England's Elijah Ponder picked up and returned for a touchdown.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye wasn't great either, completing 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, with no touchdown and one interception. But the Patriots got 76 rushing yards from TreVeyon Henderson and 43 rushing yards from Rhamondre Stevenson, and that was enough to control the game on a day when the Steelers' offense kept punting.

The Patriots and Steelers are both 1-1 through two weeks, but the Patriots have to feel a lot better about where they are going. The Steelers look like they're going nowhere.

item.title: Shane Steichen defends decisions to kick off, kick field goal in overtime
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Colts lost 33-30 in overtime after giving the Chiefs the ball first, then settling for a field goal on their own possession.
item.content:encoded:
Colts coach Shane Steichen chose to kick in Sunday night's overtime loss to the Chiefs. Questioned about those decisions after the game, Steichen defended his process even though his team lost the game.

Steichen's two choices came when the Colts won the coin toss and chose to kick off to start overtime, and then when the Colts settled for a game-tying field goal rather than trying to score a game-winning touchdown at the end of their only overtime possession.

On the choice to kick off after winning the toss, Steichen said he didn't want to score first because it would be too easy for Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to move the ball down the field if the Chiefs knew they were going to go for it on every fourth down.

"If we go first with it, Mahomes gets four downs going the other way, so we wanted to play defense there and know we had four downs," Steichen said. "It can go either way in those situations, but we decided to kick off there, and we had a chance at the end. Didn't finish it."

On the Chiefs' opening possession, they kicked a field goal. That meant on the Colts' possession, a touchdown would win the game, while a field goal would tie it and give the ball back to the Chiefs. The Colts marched down the field and faced a fourth-and-8 at the Chiefs' 15-yard line, and Steichen initially kept his offense on the field, appearing ready to go for the win. But after seeing how the Chiefs' defense lined up, Steichen told his offense to take a delay of game penalty and settled for a field goal.

"It was fourth-and-8, had a play called, had to love the look to run it there, and if not, we took the delay of game there and kicked the field goal there to tie it," Steichen said.

That tied the game 30-30, and Mahomes proceeded to move the Chiefs into field goal range, where Harrison Butker's kick gave Kansas City the 33-30 win. Steichen thinks he made the right choices, even if he doesn't like the result.

item.title: Key overtime ruling in Colts-Chiefs ignored the "clear and obvious" standard
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Chiefs should have won the game after LaQuon Treadwell's fumble.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL centralized replay review in order to ensure that a consistent standard will apply when a second look is being taken at rulings on the field. And the consistent standard is, or should be, that the available evidence makes it "clear and obvious" that the officials got it wrong in real time.

Sometimes, that standard applies. Sometimes, it doesn't.

When it comes to the play that gave the Colts a chance to beat the Chiefs in overtime, it didn't.

It wasn't clear and obvious that the officials made a mistake when ruling that Colts receiver Laquon Treadwell had caught the ball, landed on a knee/leg without being touched, and fumbled. The key question was whether Treadwell was down by contact. Which required a frame-by-frame review as to whether he had been touched by Chiefs cornerback L'Jarius Sneed after Treadwell satisfied the multi-step process of making the catch.

It was not clear and obvious that Sneed had touched Treadwell after Treadwell had completed the act of catching the ball. The fact that nearly three minutes passed from the announcement by referee Craig Wrolstad of the ruling on the field and the issuance of the final verdict shows that it was not clear and obvious.

The standard often has been summed up like this — the ruling on the field should be overturned by replay only if 50 drunks in a bar would have agreed that a mistake had been made.

Here's what is clear and obvious: Whoever made the decision in New York re-officiated the play from scratch, straining to conclude that Sneed was still contacting Treadwell after Treadwell had secured possession of the ball.

The league got lucky that the Colts opted not to attack the end zone after getting an unwarranted reprieve. Ultimately, the league got lucky that the Chiefs won the game. If they had lost, it would have been a much bigger deal.

It should still be a big deal, because it exposes the presence of a flaw in the replay machinery. The standard is "clear and obvious." It was not "clear and obvious" that the ruling on the field was incorrect. The game should have been over.

And here's the next-level take. Given the persistent belief in some circles that the league and the officials favor the Chiefs, did the person who made the final decision on replay review (whoever it was) err on the side of making a finding that runs counter to the narrative, if only to avoid a Monday news cycle that would have included more than a few people spouting off the theory that, yet again, the NFL had found a way to help the Chiefs?

Regardless of how it happened and why it happened and who specifically was responsible for it happening, the league in this instance did not honor the standard that is supposed to apply to replay review. The ruling on the field did not amount to a "clear and obvious" mistake. The game should have ended with the ruling that Treadwell had made the catch and fumbled the ball.

item.title: Dak Prescott: "Super honored" to set Cowboys TD record, want to double it
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Dak Prescott owned most of the career quarterbacking records for the Cowboys before Sunday's game against the Commanders kicked off and he broke one of the other ones late in the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
Dak Prescott owned most of the career quarterbacking records for the Cowboys before Sunday's game against the Commanders kicked off and he broke one of the other ones late in the fourth quarter.

Prescott's 24-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb was the 249th of his career, which broke a tie with Tony Romo for the most of any player in Cowboys history. It also put the finishing touches on a 37-20 Cowboys win and Prescott discussed how much the record means to him while wearing a Roger Staubach jersey at his postgame press conference.

Prescott also said he hopes to add a lot more touchdowns to the ledger before he's done in Dallas.

"I'm blessed, honored," Prescott said, via the team's website. "As I told you earlier in the week, records are meant to be broken. This is my time to break this one. Pretty cool to do it against the team I threw my first touchdown against ten years ago or so. Definitely humbling, something I don't take for granted. The great history of this organization, of the past quarterbacks before me. . . . Super, super honored. Super thankful. God's great. Not taking it lightly. But as I told you, it's just the beginning. I want to double it and plan to play for a while, so just getting started."

Prescott's place in the franchise record book will be secure regardless of what happens from here, but his place in the history of the franchise overall is still lacking the signature postseason wins that predecessors like Staubach and Troy Aikman have in their bios. Sunday's win doesn't rank at that level, but it helps the Cowboys' bid to get Prescott in position to deliver one.

item.title: Broncos think Jaylen Waddle's big day "only the tip of the iceberg"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Broncos traded for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason in order to add more explosiveness to their offense, but Waddle wasn't able to make a difference in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos traded for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason in order to add more explosiveness to their offense, but Waddle wasn't able to make a difference in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.

Week 2 provided more proof of the concept that the Broncos had in mind. Waddle had five catches of at least 14 yards, including a 49-yard leaping grab over a defender to set up Denver's first points of the day in the second quarter. Waddle wound up with eight catches for 138 yards as the Broncos came back from 10 points down to beat the Jaguars 20-13 at home on Sunday.

Head coach Sean Payton said Waddle's impact on the game was "significant" and fellow wideout Courtland Sutton said that he thinks even bigger things are coming.

"I think that's only the tip of the iceberg for him," Sutton said, via the team's website. "We have more plays in our back pocket that we didn't even get to get to. And for him to be able go out there and do what he did and us be able to have the success, and him being able to go and put together a very efficient day today, it was very promising. And I look forward to seeing where that goes the rest of the season."

The first seven quarters of the Broncos' season produced 16 points and 444 yards, which set the stage for a lot of hand-wringing about the state of the offense if the fourth quarter on Sunday went in a similar direction. The Broncos picked up 124 yards and 14 points to pull out the win, which makes it easier to talk about the brightness of a future with Waddle playing a central role in the passing game.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: We showed we can do everything offensively
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chiefs cruised to a win in their season opener against the Broncos thanks in large part to running back Kenneth Walker's big night and they moved to 2-0 in a much closer game against the Colts on Sunday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs cruised to a win in their season opener against the Broncos thanks in large part to running back Kenneth Walker's big night and they moved to 2-0 in a much closer game against the Colts on Sunday night.

Walker shone again in the 33-30 overtime victory and finished the game with 178 yards from scrimmage. The big difference with the Chiefs offense this time around was that quarterback Patrick Mahomes joined him in putting up big numbers.

Mahomes threw for 382 yards, which is his most in a game since the 2023 season, and Walker was one of five players to catch at least four passes over the course of the night. After the game, Mahomes said that Walker's presence has helped open things up offensively for the Chiefs in all phases because of how much stress the defense is under from snap to snap.

"It's fun for me," Mahomes said. "Him running the ball, our offensive line driving off the ball the way they're driving off — it's making the defense have to account for that. If not, we're going to run the ball for 200 yards or whatever we did the week before. You want to be able to do it all. We showcased that we can throw the ball down the field, we can play action and can also still run the ball. I thought coach [Andy] Reid and coach [Eric] Bieniemy did a great job calling the game, mixing it in everywhere so they couldn’t get a good gauge on what we were doing.”

The Chiefs will have to go on the road for the first time next weekend, although they'll be heading to Miami to face the 0-2 Dolphins and that should provide the offense with an opportunity to keep things rolling at a high level.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes tried to take advantage when Colts' captain didn't know OT coin toss rule
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL is in its second year of its current overtime format, but some players still haven't learned the rules.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is in its second year of its current overtime format, but some players still haven't learned the rules. And Chiefs captain Patrick Mahomes tried to take advantage of that on Sunday night.

Colts captain Cam Bynum called tails on the overtime coin toss, and when it came up tails, he had the choice to kick, receive or pick a goal to defend. But Bynum chose none of those, instead saying "defer."

Deferring is only an option for the pre-game coin toss, when the team that wins the toss can choose to defer its choice of kicking or receiving until the second half kickoff. Deferring is not an option before overtime.

As soon as Mahomes heard Bynum's mistake, he yelled to referee Craig Wrolstad, "They get the ball!" Mahomes figured that if Bynum was going to defer the Colts' choice, then the Chiefs would make their choice, which was to kick off and get the ball second in overtime.

Unfortunately for Mahomes, Wrolstad asked Bynum follow-up questions until Bynum understood.

"Would you like the ball? Would you like the ball? Would you like to play defense?" Wrolstad asked Bynum.

Eventually, Bynum said the Colts wanted to start on defense — which is technically not a choice at the start of overtime, but Wrolstad knew Bynum meant the Colts wanted to kick off, and Wrolstad accepted that.

"Indianapolis won the toss, they would like to play defense," Wrolstad announced to the crowd.

After the game, Mahomes confirmed that he was trying to take advantage of Bynum's mistake.

"You're supposed to say kick off. You can't defer in overtime. If you defer, then it's my decision. So I was like, then I want to kick off," Mahomes said. "You're supposed to say kick off, he said defer, so I said, Well, I'll kick off then. That's the rules, I guess, but it didn't work."

Mahomes credited Mike Frazier, the Chiefs' longtime statistical analysis coordinator, for making sure the Chiefs' players always know exactly what their options are in such situations. Mahomes knew the rule, and Bynum didn't.

item.title: Initial hope is that Caleb Williams has a Grade 1 hamstring strain
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It looked bad.
item.content:encoded:
It looked bad. It ultimately could be much better than the Bears could have hoped for.

Quarterback Caleb Williams will have an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of his hamstring injury. There's currently optimism that it's not serious.

The hope, we're told, is that it will be diagnosed as a Grade 1 injury. That's the lowest level, with minimal tearing of the muscle fibers.

Ultimately, the MRI will show the extent of the injury. And even if it's only a Grade 1 strain, it's possible he won't be ready to go in eight days, when the Bears host the Eagles on Monday Night Football.

If Williams can't go, it will be Tyson Bagent. Who performed well in limited duty on Sunday, and in whom the Bears have a high degree of confidence.

Bagent started four games as a rookie in 2023, winning two of them. Last year, the new coaching staff led by Ben Johnson opted to sign Bagent to a two-year, $10 million extension.

item.title: Travis Hunter played 60 percent of Jaguars' defensive snaps, 10 percent of offensive snaps
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a part-time player on defense and a bit player on offense in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a part-time player on defense and a bit player on offense in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.

Hunter played 37 snaps (60 percent of the Jaguars' plays) on defense, six snaps (10 percent) on offense and one play on special teams. Although the Jaguars have talked up the possibility of Hunter being a full-time player on both sides of the ball, he's not even close to that. In fact, 17 different players on the Jaguars were on the field for more plays than Hunter's total of 44 snaps.

On defense, Hunter's highlights included four tackles, a pass breakup, and a 22-yard pass interference penalty. That penalty, and Jaguars coach Liam Coen's penalty for arguing the call, set up a Broncos touchdown. On offense, Hunter never had the ball go his way.

Hunter said he accepts his role on the team.

"That's the plan. Coaches tell me what I've got to do, I just follow their plan, follow their lead," Hunter said. "My job is to go out there and play, no matter when they put me out there. That's what I've got to do."

What Hunter is doing so far is not living up to expectations as the No. 2 overall pick in last year's draft.

item.title: DeMeco Ryans: History doesn't matter, the 2026 Texans have to play good football
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: No team wants to start a season 0-2, but the Texans would seem to be the likeliest team in the league to shrug off a sluggish start to the year.
item.content:encoded:
No team wants to start a season 0-2, but the Texans would seem to be the likeliest team in the league to shrug off a sluggish start to the year.

DeMeco Ryans became the team's head coach in 2023 and they went from 0-2 to the playoffs. An 0-3 start last year didn't stop them from doing the same thing and the Texans went on to win Wild Card games in each of those seasons, so one might think that would be a talking point in Houston in the wake of Sunday's 20-6 loss to the Bengals.

After Sunday's game, Ryans was asked if there's anything to take away from past seasons and he did not find any bright side.

“Nothing. We got to go to work," Ryans said at a press conference. "We got to go play good football. That's bottom line. It's nothing to look back on of what happened in the past. This team right now, [the] 2026 Texans have to dig deep, look down — all of us, look down, look deep within ourselves and see how we can find a way to play better football."

While the Texans might not take solace from history, the present is also kind to them. The Titans and Colts are also 0-2 while the Jaguars are 1-1, so it doesn't look like the division is going to be running away from them. A trip to Indianapolis is on tap in Week 3 and a win there would make for a much brighter outlook in Houston.
